correctness.rationale: All 729 component transition tables are enumerated by unique base-three codes. For each, all 126 words of length 1–6 are evaluated directly on the three starting states; independent subset reachability verifies all 180 no-reset cases and proves the other 549 have short resets. For all 549² ordered synchronizable pairs, direct word-set intersection gives the six exact counts; a separate C++ subset-pair BFS reproduces the same counts and checks shortestness with no word-length cutoff. Symmetry relabeling enumerates 11 extremal orbits, and a fully stated six-letter witness has no common shorter reset. This is a complete finite proof, not an infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: A full reading of the mathematical product definitions, product reset-language identity and general threshold bounds in Fernau–Rystsov (arXiv:2611.09136v1, §§2–3,7) yields no exact three-state binary pair spectrum; those results bound each pair between the maximum and sum of the individual thresholds. Volkov (Russian Mathematical Surveys 77(5), §§2–3) provides the individual three-state sharp bound four and subset search, but not a pair-product distribution. A published separate record treating standard Černý automata through eleven states addresses a proper family with distinct parameters and does not imply the all-binary-table classification; its full text could not be checked. The present full 301401-pair distribution and eleven orbit types were not found in the actually inspected relevant material; this is best-knowledge originality, not an assertion of uniqueness against all possible publications.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased exact finite classification may exist; a negative search is not proof of priority.
Full documents behind two related published finite-record summaries could not be inspected, so no whole-document noncoverage is asserted.
The result is finite and computational, not a general product reset theorem for larger automata.

value.rationale: The motivating product automata literature poses exact bound-attainment and shared-control questions. For the natural first nontrivial equal-sized component domain, the generic bound 8 is not sharp: the exact 6 threshold and a 301401-pair distribution quantify how often common-input delay occurs. Eleven extremal symmetry types classify all worst cases; these are not an arbitrary subset or a recomputation of an available table. The precise finite cutoff, spectrum, and extremal structure are mathematically meaningful independently of larger-state asymptotics.
